title: Purdue faculty innovates in AI, quantum computing and software security
byline: Armin Moin innovates in AI, quantum computing and software security
excerpt: Armin Moin, Assistant Professor in Purdue Polytechnic Institute's School of Applied and Creative Computing, is advancing research at the intersection of artificial intelligence, software engineering and quantum computing.
content:
Armin Moin, Assistant Professor in Purdue Polytechnic Institute's School of Applied and Creative Computing, is advancing research at the intersection of artificial intelligence, software engineering and quantum computing.

Moin directs the Purdue Quantum-Classical AI and Software Engineering (QCASE) Lab, which operates across Purdue's West Lafayette and Indianapolis locations. His research explores how artificial intelligence can improve software development, strengthen security, and address complex technological challenges, as well as how software should be developed for emerging platforms, namely quantum computers.

The lab's research focuses on four interconnected areas: artificial intelligence for software engineering, software engineering for artificial intelligence, quantum software engineering, and software security.

Moin also emphasizes research mentoring and training, providing opportunities for undergraduate and graduate students to participate in research. His work connects technical innovation with applications in industry and mentoring opportunities for students to develop their own ventures.

During an Oct. 29 presentation at Purdue University in Indianapolis, Moin introduced the Purdue QCASE Lab's research program and its emphasis on student mentorship, industry engagement, and community impact.
